task.title: Regression: slugify keeps separator runs and edge hyphens
task.statement: Regression report for slugkit.slugify(text). Since the last change the function returns 'hello--world' for 'Hello--World', 'a---b' for 'a -- b' and 'end-' for 'end!'. The intended behaviour, which the existing tests only partly cover, is: lower-case the text; every maximal run of one or more characters that are not ASCII letters a-z or ASCII digits 0-9 becomes exactly one hyphen; leading and trailing hyphens are removed; an input with no ASCII letters or digits (including the empty string and whitespace-only text) returns ''. Non-ASCII letters such as 'é' are separators, not kept characters (so 'café crème' is 'caf-cr-me'). Keep raising TypeError for non-string input, keep returning a str, and keep the existing tests in tests/ passing without modifying them. Fix the regression in slugkit/core.py.
acceptance_criteria: slugify('Hello--World') == 'hello-world', slugify('a -- b') == 'a-b', slugify('one , two ; three') == 'one-two-three', slugify('x___y') == 'x-y' (runs of separators collapse to one hyphen).
slugify('end!') == 'end', slugify('  padded  ') == 'padded', slugify('--both--') == 'both', slugify('(parens)') == 'parens' (no leading or trailing hyphen).
slugify('') == '', slugify('!!!') == '', slugify('   ') == '' (nothing to keep gives the empty string).

Existing behaviour is preserved: slugify('Hello World') == 'hello-world', slugify('already-a-slug') == 'already-a-slug', slugify('Python 3') == 'python-3', slugify('MiXeD CaSe 42') == 'mixed-case-42'.
Non-ASCII letters are separators: slugify('café crème') == 'caf-cr-me' and slugify('日本語') == ''.
The result is a str; TypeError for non-string input such as None, 3, 2.5, ['a'] and b'bytes'.

spec.restated_task: Fix slugkit/core.py so slugify converts ASCII uppercase letters to lowercase, preserves ASCII letters and digits, replaces each maximal run of all other characters with one hyphen, and removes edge hyphens. interface_contract.name: slugkit.slugify
interface_contract.behavior: Accept a str, including str subclasses, and return a str. Retain original ASCII letters A-Z and a-z and ASCII digits 0-9, converting A-Z to a-z. Treat every other character, including existing hyphens, underscores, whitespace, punctuation, and non-ASCII characters, as a separator. Replace each maximal separator run with exactly one hyphen, then remove leading and trailing hyphens. Return '' when nothing remains. To resolve Unicode casing ambiguity, determine ASCII eligibility from the original characters: non-ASCII characters remain separators even if Unicode lowercasing could produce ASCII characters. The function remains accessible through both slugkit.slugify and slugkit.core.slugify.
error_cases: TypeError: text is not an instance of str; preserve the existing message 'text must be a str'.

acceptance_criteria: 1. Separator runs collapse: 'Hello--World' returns 'hello-world'; 'a -- b' returns 'a-b'; 'one , two ; three' returns 'one-two-three'; 'x___y' returns 'x-y'.
2. Edge separators disappear: 'end!' returns 'end'; '  padded  ' returns 'padded'; '--both--' returns 'both'; '(parens)' returns 'parens'.
4. Existing normal behavior is preserved: 'Hello World' returns 'hello-world'; 'already-a-slug' returns 'already-a-slug'; 'Python 3' returns 'python-3'; 'MiXeD CaSe 42' returns 'mixed-case-42'.
5. Non-ASCII characters are separators: 'café crème' returns 'caf-cr-me'; '日本語' returns ''; 'aé日b' returns 'a-b'; non-ASCII digits such as '１２٣' return ''.
6. Non-ASCII characters are not converted into retained ASCII letters through Unicode casing: 'K' returns ''; 'İ' returns ''; 'aKb' returns 'a-b'.
7. ASCII letters and digits are retained in order with only ASCII uppercase letters lowercased: 'AZaz019' returns 'azaz019'.
8. Every successful result is a str and is either empty or consists of nonempty lowercase ASCII alphanumeric groups separated by single hyphens.
9. None, 3, 2.5, ['a'], and b'bytes' each raise TypeError with message 'text must be a str'.
10. A str subclass instance containing 'Hello--World' is accepted and produces 'hello-world'.
11. Both public import paths continue to expose slugify(text), supporting positional and text keyword arguments.
12. All existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing ones changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception raised in the code under test is never overridden (only a test-internal crash or a timeout may be corrected).
